info.name: Cherry API - Accounting Integration
info.description:
API collection for managing company accounting settings and workflow configurations.

This collection allows companies to:
- Configure when transactions hit the accounting system
- Choose between accrual and cash basis accounting
- Set up approval workflows
- Manage account code mappings

request.description:
Retrieves the current accounting settings for the authenticated user's company.

Returns:
- Current settings configuration
- Available options for all configurable fields
- Trigger options for sales, purchases, and expenses

request.description:
Updates the accounting settings for the authenticated user's company.

**Available Fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| accounting_method | string | `accrual` or `cash` |
| sales_recognition_trigger | string | When to record sales (see options below) |
| purchase_recognition_trigger | string | When to record purchases |
| expense_recognition_trigger | string | When to record expenses |
| auto_record_cash_sales | boolean | Auto-record POS/cash sales |
| auto_record_customer_payments | boolean | Auto-record customer payments |
| auto_record_supplier_payments | boolean | Auto-record supplier payments |
| require_expense_approval | boolean | Require approval for expenses |
| expense_approval_threshold | number | Amount above which approval is required |
| accounting_integration_enabled | boolean | Enable/disable accounting integration |

**Sales Recognition Triggers:**
- `order_created` - When order is created
- `order_completed` - When order is completed
- `order_dispatched` - When order is dispatched
- `order_delivered` - When delivery is confirmed
- `invoice_created` - When invoice is created
- `invoice_sent` - When invoice is sent (default)
- `invoice_approved` - When invoice is approved
- `payment_received` - When payment is received (cash basis)

Example: Configure company for cash basis accounting.

In cash basis accounting:
- Revenue is recorded when payment is received
- Expenses are recorded when payment is made
- No accounts receivable/payable tracking

Example: Configure company to record revenue when delivery is confirmed through the dispatch process.

This is useful for:
- Companies that need proof of delivery before recognizing revenue
- Businesses with high return rates
- Compliance with revenue recognition standards (ASC 606)

Example: Temporarily disable automatic accounting integration.

When disabled:
- No automatic journal entries are created
- Business transactions still process normally
- Manual journal entries can still be created

Resets all accounting settings to their default values.

**Default Configuration:**
- Accounting Method: Accrual
- Sales Trigger: Invoice Sent
- Purchase Trigger: Goods Received
- Expense Trigger: Expense Approved
- Auto-record payments: Enabled
- Require expense approval: Enabled

Returns a plain-language summary of the current accounting configuration.

Useful for:
- Displaying settings to non-technical users
- Dashboard widgets
- Configuration review

item.name: Account Mappings
item.description: Manage chart of account mappings for different transaction types

request.description:
Lists all account mappings configured for the company.

Account mappings link business transaction types to specific Chart of Account codes.

Returns all available mapping keys that can be configured.

**Core Keys:**
- sales_revenue
- accounts_receivable
- accounts_payable
- cash
- bank
- vat_output
- vat_input
- cost_of_goods_sold
- inventory
- general_expense

**Payment Method Keys:**
- payment_cash
- payment_card
- payment_bank_transfer
- payment_mpesa
Creates a new account mapping for a specific transaction type.

Updates multiple account mappings in a single request.

Useful for initial setup or bulk configuration changes.

Initializes default account mappings based on the company's existing Chart of Accounts.

This attempts to auto-match accounts by:
- Account code patterns (e.g., 4xxx for income)
- Account names (e.g., 'Sales Revenue')
- Account types

Validates the current account mapping configuration.

Returns:
- Missing required mappings
- Invalid account references
- Configuration warnings

item.name: Business Workflows
item.description: Examples of how accounting entries are triggered by business operations

request.description:
Sends an invoice to the customer.

**Accounting Trigger:** If `sales_recognition_trigger` is set to `invoice_sent`, this creates:

```
DR Accounts Receivable    $X,XXX
    CR Sales Revenue              $X,XXX
    CR VAT Output (if applicable) $XXX
```

Records a payment against an invoice.

**Accounting Entry (Accrual Basis):**
```
DR Bank/Cash              $X,XXX
    CR Accounts Receivable        $X,XXX
```

**Accounting Entry (Cash Basis):**
If `sales_recognition_trigger` is `payment_received`:
```
DR Bank/Cash              $X,XXX
    CR Sales Revenue              $X,XXX
```

Marks a dispatch as delivered (delivery confirmation).

**Accounting Trigger:** If `sales_recognition_trigger` is set to `order_delivered`, this creates:

```
DR Accounts Receivable    $X,XXX
    CR Sales Revenue              $X,XXX
```

This is useful for companies that want to recognize revenue only when delivery is confirmed.

Approves an expense.

**Accounting Trigger:** If `expense_recognition_trigger` is set to `expense_approved`, this creates:

```
DR Expense Account        $X,XXX
    CR Cash/Bank                  $X,XXX
```
